proposals.before: In Chengsheng year 3 (553) he was made bright-prestige general and roaming-cavalry general, raised to marquis with five hundred households.
proposals.after: In Chengsheng year 3 (554) he was made bright-prestige general and roaming-cavalry general, raised to marquis with five hundred households.
proposals.reason: Chengsheng 1 began in AD 552, so year 3 is AD 554, not 553.

proposals.before: Xiao Bo sent Ouyang Bao against him. Faqu met him in battle and broke his force.
proposals.after: Xiao Bo sent Ouyang He against him. Faqu met him in battle and broke his force.
proposals.reason: 歐陽頠 is Ouyang He (He/Wei), not Bao; the given name was mistranslated.

proposals.before: Xiao Bo sent Ouyang Bao to attack Faqu; Faqu fought him and defeated him.
proposals.after: Xiao Bo sent Ouyang He to attack Faqu; Faqu fought him and defeated him.
proposals.reason: Matches the idiomatic repair: 頠 is He, not Bao.

proposals.before: In the second year of Yongding, Wang Lin sent Li Xiaoqin, Fan Meng, and Yu Xiaoxiang to attack Zhou Di and also plotted to capture Faqu; Faqu led troops to aid Di and captured Xiaoxiang and three other generals.
proposals.after: In the second year of Yongding, Wang Lin sent Li Xiaoqin, Fan Meng, and Yu Xiaoxiang to attack Zhou Di and also plotted to capture Faqu; Faqu led troops to aid Di and captured Xiaoxiang and the three generals.
proposals.reason: 孝頃等三將 means the three generals (including Xiaoxiang), not three others besides him.

proposals.before: When Emperor Wen took the throne, Faqu's title was raised to pacify-south general.
proposals.after: When Emperor Wen took the throne, Faqu's title was raised to secure-south general.
proposals.reason: 安南將軍 is distinct from earlier 平南將軍; both were collapsed to "pacify-south".

proposals.before: In Tianjia year 2 (563) Zhou Di rebelled. Faqu led his men to join area commander Wu Mingche and fought Di at Gongtang.
proposals.after: In Tianjia year 2 (561) Zhou Di rebelled. Faqu led his men to join area commander Wu Mingche and fought Di at Gongtang.
proposals.reason: Tianjia 1 is AD 560, so year 2 is AD 561, not 563.

proposals.before: When the Founder took the throne, Liang was made credential-holder, scattered-cavalry regular attendant, and pacify-west grand general, with pipes and drums and his command and inspectorship unchanged.
proposals.after: When the Founder received the abdication, Liang was made credential-holder, scattered-cavalry regular attendant, and pacify-west grand general, with pipes and drums and his command and inspectorship unchanged.
proposals.reason: 受禪 means receiving the abdication; the Chinese 襌 is the common 禪/襌 confusion, but English should preserve abdication sense as in the literal.

proposals.before: When Jiao was pacified, he also reduced Zhou general the Senior Duke Tuo Ba Ding and others.
proposals.after: When Jiao was pacified, he also reduced Zhou general the Senior Duke Tuoba Ding and others.
proposals.reason: 拓跋 is the ethnonym Tuoba, not spaced Tuo Ba.
沌 is Dun, not Chun; the collation notes distinguish 沌口 (Dun Ford) from 柵口.
Literal likewise romanizes 沌 as Chun; should be Dun.
Same 沌 graph; collation discusses 沌口 versus 柵口.
Same romanization error for 沌 in the collation lemma.

decisions.reason: 承聖三年 with Chengsheng 1 = AD 552 is AD 554; the parenthetical (553) is off by one.

decisions.after: Xiao Bo sent Ouyang Wei against him. Faqu met him in battle and broke his force.
decisions.reason: 歐陽頠 is Ouyang Wei (498–563), father of 歐陽紇 Ouyang He; Bao is wrong, but the proposal would conflate father and son.

decisions.after: Xiao Bo sent Ouyang Wei to attack Faqu; Faqu fought him and defeated him.
decisions.reason: The literal field likewise requires Ouyang Wei for 歐陽頠, keeping him distinct from his son Ouyang He (歐陽紇).

decisions.after: In the second year of Yongding, Wang Lin sent Li Xiaoqin, Fan Meng, and Yu Xiaoqing to attack Zhou Di and also plotted to capture Faqu; Faqu led troops to aid Di and captured Xiaoqing and the other two generals.
decisions.reason: 孝頃等三將 means Xiaoqing and the other two generals, three total; 頃 is qing, so 余孝頃 is Yu Xiaoqing rather than Yu Xiaoxiang.
安南將軍 is a different title from the earlier 平南將軍; collapsing both to "pacify-south" erases the advancement. "secure-south" restores the distinction.
天嘉二年 with Tianjia 1 = AD 560 is AD 561; the parenthetical (563) is wrong.
受襌 (for 受禪) means receiving the abdication, not a generic "took the throne"; the proposed wording matches the Chinese technical sense and the literal.
拓跋 is the single ethnonym Tuoba; spacing it as Tuo Ba invents a two-part personal name.
沌 is Dun (as in 沌口); Chun is the wrong romanization for this graph.
Literal likewise misreads 沌 as Chun; Dun is the correct reading.
Collation lemma 沌 is again Dun, not Chun; the repair matches the graph.
Same collation unit: 沌 romanizes as Dun; Chun is incorrect in the literal field too.

claimRevisions.reason: The corrected translation identifies 歐陽頠 as Ouyang Wei, not his son Ouyang He.
The corrected translation restores the reading of 頃 as qing in 余孝頃.
